input: nums is a nonempty Array of n integers in [-100,100], with 1 <= n <= 10000; k is an integer in [0,10000]. k=0 is an explicit extension. Integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Numbers, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays without holes, subclasses, proxies or accessors; strings are primitive. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not dynamically validated. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The maximum array sum attainable after exactly k operations, each replacing one chosen occurrence by its negation. An occurrence may be selected repeatedly. Return the sum only; nums itself is not changed.
mutation_aliasing: A private sorted copy is modified when negative values are flipped. Caller values, ordering and all caller aliases remain unchanged. Remaining even flips are modeled as cancelling pairs, not executed against any container. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state.
numeric: Negated values stay in [-100,100]. The absolute sum of n values is at most 1000000; the final evaluated subtraction of twice the smallest absolute value has conservative intermediate magnitude at most 1000200. k decreases only while positive. All arithmetic and comparator differences are exact safe integers.
complexity: After sorting, O(n) work flips negative values from smallest upward and scans the resulting values for sum and minimum absolute value. If residual k is odd, one minimum-magnitude occurrence accounts for the final necessary flip; arbitrary remaining pairs cancel. JavaScript copied sorting adds O(n+1) copying plus target-runtime T_sort(n) comparison/sort work and S_sort(n) workspace. ECMAScript supplies no universal O(n log n) sort complexity guarantee; comparator work is bounded O(1) here and is included in T_sort.
